questions.question: Which of the following is a key physical property of rock regarding its transition to a liquid state?
options: Its melting point is extremely high.
Its melting point is identical to that of water.
It easily melts at room temperature.
Its melting point is extremely low, below 0 degrees Celsius.

questions.question: What is molten rock called when it is located underground beneath the Earth's surface?
options: Lava
Magma
Obsidian
Basalt

questions.question: Where does intrusive igneous rock form?
options: On the surface of the Earth's crust
Inside the Earth's crust
On top of glaciers
Inside the liquid outer core

questions.question: What factor directly determines the size of the crystals that form in a cooling rock?
options: The rate at which the melted rock cools
The amount of water present in the atmosphere
The color of the surrounding soil
The volume of air above the volcano

questions.question: Rocks are composed of grains, which can have what types of shapes or arrangements?
options: Liquid or gaseous
Round or interlocking
Square or hollow
Metallic or fibrous

questions.question: How are the atoms arranged inside a crystal substance?
options: In a completely random and chaotic manner
In a very regular, repeating pattern
In loose, moving liquid droplets
In a hollow sphere with no internal bonds

questions.question: Under what conditions do metamorphic rocks form, causing their original structures to alter?
options: Freezing temperatures and low atmospheric pressure at sea level
Extreme pressure and high temperature
Rapid cooling in ocean water with no pressure
Dissolving in rainwater over a very short time

questions.question: What are the primary constituents that make up a rock?
options: Minerals and rock fragments
Water and organic leaves
Pure liquid metals and gases
Plastic fibers and synthetic chemicals

questions.question: What is a mineral?
options: A man-made mixture of various liquid elements
A naturally occurring pure substance with a crystal structure
Any rock that contains fossils of ancient animals
A liquid compound found only in the Earth's atmosphere

questions.question: Which dense, rocky layer lies directly beneath the Earth's thin crust?
options: The inner core
The outer core
The mantle
The atmosphere

questions.question: What is the structure of the Earth's core at the very centre of the planet?
options: A liquid metallic core surrounded by a solid outer core
A solid metallic core surrounded by a liquid outer core
A completely gaseous chamber surrounded by solid rock
A hollow sphere filled with liquid water

questions.question: Why is the inner core of the Earth solid despite its extremely high temperature?
options: Because temperature decreases towards the centre
Because pressure decreases towards the centre
Because temperature and pressure both increase towards the centre
Because the inner core is made of frozen ice

questions.question: How is the Earth's crust structured, and how do its pieces behave?
options: It is a single, solid, immovable shell.
It is broken into tectonic plates that move very, very slowly.
It is made of liquid plates that flow like rivers.
It is broken into plates that spin rapidly every day.

questions.question: What is a key structural feature of sedimentary rocks?
options: They contain distinct grains that are stuck together.
They are made of liquid metal that has cooled instantly.
They consist entirely of perfectly aligned large crystals.
They are formed from rapidly cooled lava on the Earth's surface.

questions.question: How do the crystal arrangements of igneous and metamorphic rocks compare?
options: Both rock types contain crystals that align perfectly in one direction.
Igneous rocks have crystals pointing in many directions, while metamorphic rocks contain crystals that mostly line up.
Metamorphic rocks have crystals pointing in many directions, while igneous rocks contain crystals that mostly line up.
Neither rock type contains any crystal structures.
